title: Cloud Network Traffic Volume Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.6.5 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.6.5 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (VPC Flow Logs), Azure NSG flow logs; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS (VPC Flow Logs), Azure NSG flow logs
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.5_cloud_network_traffic_vo_5"
| sort -_time
description: Weekly VPC flow log volume indicates shifting traffic patterns, DDoS aftermath, or misconfigured mirroring. Complements per-flow analysis with a coarse health signal and correlates with network-related cost changes.
value: Detecting cloud network traffic volume trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Parse VPC Flow or NSG flow fields so bytes is numeric. Filter internal-only noise if needed via RFC1918 CIDR lists. Use weekly buckets for medium-term trending; index volume growth also correlates with ingest cost. For Azure, map to the appropriate custom sourcetype for raw flows. Alert on sudden jumps exceeding 2x the 4-week moving average.
visualization: Column chart (weekly total GB), line overlay (4-week SMA), dual axis with flow record count.
knownFalsePositives: Inventories can skip a run when an API is throttled or a connector is in maintenance, which looks like a big drop. We check the ingest time and the last good snapshot before we call it shrinkage.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (VPC Flow Logs), Azure NSG flow logs with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Parse VPC Flow or NSG flow fields so bytes is numeric. Filter internal-only noise if needed via RFC1918 CIDR lists. Use weekly buckets for medium-term trending; index volume growth also correlates with ingest cost. For Azure, map to the appropriate custom sourcetype for raw flows. Alert on sudden jumps exceeding 2x the 4-week moving average.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.5_cloud_network_traffic_vo_5"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:vpcflow` in `index=cloud` to detect cloud network traffic volume trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_5_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Column chart (weekly total GB), line overlay (4-week SMA), dual axis with flow record count..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (VPC Flow Logs), Azure NSG flow logs and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud network traffic volume trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
